checked_decisions.finding: Baldora Charge near-critical / area-suppression priority for Ensign Barrel's access both preserved; 'Baldora Charge' term accepted per orchestrator ruling.

Freezemouth self-address monologue ('this cursed self of mine... let's end it here') correctly kept as an unattributed plain statement; matches Berkt's later confession (9276-9292) in content only, no name inserted into the row itself.
'We... didn't make it, did we' correctly mirrors source (私たち……だめでしたね, no named referent); left neutral, no speaker/subject invented.
'Damn Berkt... to think he prepared this many' matches source exactly; Berkt named by source itself (not inferred).
'Clear a path for Barrel and Faye' / 'Send Barrel and Faye forward' both match source's explicit naming of both pilots; no third identity added.

Source names only 輝 (Hikaru, given name, no surname) and 先輩 (senpai/senior). Target text 'Hikaru!' and 'senior' carries no surname or gender and is correct regardless of which Hikaru is meant, so no fix to the target is needed. However, the translator's supporting note is unsound: it identifies this as Hikaru Ichijyo (Macross) using 'adjacent finale content in resource 6281-6282', but resource 6281 is a separate, unrelated scene (confirmed by batch_09375's own footer note: row 9388 begins resource 6281, the Macross DYRL finale, out of this mission's scope). character_names_021.json in fact has two candidates: Hikaru Ichijyo (Macross, male) and Hikaru Amano (Nadesico, female, confirmed on the Nadesico wiki). Given this whole scene (resource 6280) is saturated with Nadesico context - the ship 'Nadesico' itself under attack, Harry/Hari Makibi addressed by name, a 'senpai' address matching Nadesico's cast dynamics - Hikaru Amano is at least as plausible as Hikaru Ichijyo, arguably more so. No identity is asserted in the translated text, so this is a correction to the review record only, not a target edit.

Barrel/Berkt confrontation is untagged in source but internally self-identifying: 'Berkt' and 'Barrel' are each addressed by name within the exchange, and content (who claims 'you took everything from me', who says 'I carried the name Barrel') consistently sorts the two speakers. Attribution notes in the batch are inferential, not asserted as fact in the target text; agreed as reasonable and unforced. Row 9283's plural 貴様ら correctly rendered as 'all of you' rather than singular.

'My hatred is directed at your very existence' adds 'your' where source only says 存在そのもの (existence itself). This is contextually settled, not invented: the entire exchange is direct address between Berkt and Barrel, and 9287-9288 explicitly confirm the hatred targets Barrel by name/face. Acceptable.
Polite 'anata' (9282) and feminine sentence-ending の (9286) correctly left unassigned to either Barrel or Faye; translation does not force an identity the source doesn't settle.

'Because I carried the name Barrel, I had to suffer' keeps Barrel and Berkt as distinct speaker identities per glossary guidance (char.barrel_orland note on parallel-world identities); no merge performed.
